## Identification resources

Accurate species identification is essential for every analysis that uses the camera-trap database.

Our project uses several wildlife identification guides originally developed through **eMammal**, a platform that supported camera-trap projects and has since transitioned toward Wildlife Insights.

### Recommended guides

1. [Snapshot USA Common Mammals Guide](https://emammal.si.edu/sites/default/files/2024-06/snapshot-usa-complete-field-guide.pdf)
2. [Guide to Identifying Deer](https://emammal.si.edu/sites/default/files/2024-06/ft-deer_id_guide_0.pdf)
3. [Guide to Identifying Eastern Squirrels](https://emammal.si.edu/sites/default/files/2024-06/squirrel-id-training.pdf)
4. [Guide to Identifying Canids](https://emammal.si.edu/sites/default/files/2024-06/ft-canid_id_guide.pdf)

Additional project-specific guides can be added to this page as new identification needs arise.

## Classification rule

::: {.callout-important}
### If you are unsure, do not guess

The quality of every research product produced from these data depends on correct species classification.

If you are uncertain about an identification:

1. classify the record as **Unknown**;
2. add a comment describing what made the identification difficult; and
3. flag the image for later review when appropriate.

Never assign a species simply because it appears to be the most likely option.
:::

## Why identification quality matters

Errors introduced during image classification propagate into every later stage of the project, including:

- species lists;
- detection counts;
- activity-pattern analyses;
- event rates;
- community summaries; and
- student research projects.

Careful classification during the initial processing stage is therefore one of the most important quality-control steps in the entire camera-trap workflow.
